action.rendered_skill_text:
# Skill - Create Epic Stories

## Identity

```text
skill_id:    delivery-lead.create-epic-stories
persona:     delivery-lead
action_id:   create-epic-stories
produces:    epics/
```

## When this skill is used

Run after epic shells (`epic.md` + `implementation-contract.md`) exist for all epics. This skill generates the story files for one epic, reading the already-written contract as input.

## Role for this task

You are a senior delivery lead producing story-level specifications with full behavioral detail. You read the implementation contract that was already created and translate it into concrete, testable stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria and a paired AI-ready story contract.

## Per-item execution

This action runs once per epic. The engine provides `E-002` (the epic ID) and `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/` (the resolved epic folder path, e.g. `epics/E-002-ai-pre-screening-scoring/`).

**Always use `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/` for file paths.** Never construct the folder path from `E-002` — the folder includes a slug that only the engine knows.

- Create story files and story agent contracts ONLY for that one epic
- Do not create or modify stories for other epics
- The engine will call this action again for each remaining epic

## Preconditions

Before starting, verify that all files listed in `- planning/delivery-skeleton.md
- requirements/atomic-requirements.md
- architecture/architecture-rules.md
- architecture/solution-decisions.md
- architecture/impacted-systems.md
- governance/delivery-constitution.md
- epics/` exist and are readable.

**Critical:** the epic folder `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/` must already contain `epic.md` and `implementation-contract.md`. If either is missing, stop and report the blocker.

## Hard constraints

- **Before creating any story file, check if a file with the same story ID prefix already exists** (e.g. `S-002.0-scoring-e2e.md` for story `S-002.0`). If an existing file matches, **update it in place** — do not create a new bare-ID file alongside it. If no existing file matches, create `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/stories/S-NNN.N-<slug>.md` where `<slug>` is a short kebab-case summary of the story title (e.g. `S-001.3-application-form-ui.md`).
- Apply the same rule for agent contracts: check for existing `S-NNN.N-*.agent.yaml` before creating `S-NNN.N-<slug>.agent.yaml`.
- Every story must trace to at least one requirement
- Every story must declare a `Story Type`
- Every story must distinguish `Requirements Implemented` from `Requirements Referenced`
- Acceptance criteria MUST be in Given/When/Then Gherkin format with test type, criticality, and automation annotations
- Do NOT produce only 2 scenarios per story - most stories need 4-8 scenarios covering: happy path, validation or negative, authorization, boundary, integration failure, state transition, concurrency, and audit
- Each Gherkin scenario must use concrete values (field names, HTTP codes, entity states, thresholds from the BRS and implementation contract) - not vague outcomes
- Each AC must have a criticality tag (`[critical]`, `[important]`, `[standard]`) and automation tag (`[automate]`, `[manual]`, `[automate-later]`)
- Each story must declare which application layers it touches
- Each story must have `## Business Context`
- Each story must have `## In Scope`
- Each story must have `## Implementation Guidance` referencing the implementation contract
- Each story must have `## Dependency Contracts`
- Each story must have `## Test Expectations`
- Each story must have `## Required Tests`
- Every requirement mapped to this epic must be covered by at least one story
- **Each feature (F-NNN) from the delivery skeleton must produce at least one story.** Do NOT collapse an entire epic into a single story
- If a feature covers multiple requirements that span different application layers, consider splitting into layer-specific stories
- If `architecture/impacted-systems.md` or the epic contract shows an external integration, adapter, provider callback, or third-party dependency, create at least one **dedicated integration story** for that concern. Do NOT hide third-party integration work inside a broad e2e or platform story
- If a requirement affects an admin dashboard, operational dashboard, portal page, workflow screen, or case-management UI, create at least one **dedicated frontend or UI story** for that surface. Do NOT treat the backend endpoint story as sufficient UI coverage
- If observability, audit append, metrics, or notification concerns appear in the implementation contract as distinct surfaces, do not overload them into one generic platform story unless they are genuinely inseparable. Prefer separate implementation stories when they result in different components, contracts, or acceptance criteria
- A story classified as `spike`, `poc`, `e2e`, or `exploration` may validate feasibility, orchestration, or end-to-end flow, but it must NOT be the only story directly implementing a Must functional requirement when a non-spike implementation slice is possible
- Unresolved questions and ambiguities from the linked requirements must be carried into the relevant story `## Open Questions` section
- Do not leave placeholder text
- If `architecture/solution-decisions.md` exists: every `create-new` decision targeting this epic must result in at least one dedicated story
- If `architecture/solution-decisions.md` exists: every decision affecting an external adapter, new integration boundary, callback endpoint, dashboard page, or cross-system workflow must be reflected in story planning explicitly rather than assumed to be covered indirectly
- If solution decisions or repo context exist: each story must include a `## Technical Scope` section describing concrete work per component
- If no repository information is available at all, omit `## Technical Scope`
- If the implementation contract has a `## UI Surface` section: stories with a `Frontend` layer must include a `## UI Behaviour` section specifying which page, which fields/components the story affects, validation UX, states (loading/error/success), and user flow. Gherkin scenarios for frontend stories must test UI-level behavior (form submission, validation errors, navigation), not just API responses
- For frontend stories, `## UI Behaviour` must be derived from the epic implementation contract's `## UI Surface`. Do not invent new page-level UI facts at story level.
- If the implementation contract includes retry policy, timeout handling, fallback routing, callback validation, idempotency, state transition rules, or provider unavailability handling, at least one story must own those behaviors directly with concrete acceptance criteria
- The paired `.agent.yaml` file must be concise, structured, and self-sufficient for a coding agent. It must not merely restate the prose story.
- **Every API path in the `.agent.yaml` `implementation_contract.api` and `operations` sections must reference an endpoint defined in the epic's `implementation-contract.md`.** Do not invent API paths. If the contract defines `GET /score/{arn}`, use that exact path and method — do not write `POST /scoring/result`.

## Instructions

### Step 1 - Read inputs fully

Read every file listed in `- planning/delivery-skeleton.md
- requirements/atomic-requirements.md
- architecture/architecture-rules.md
- architecture/solution-decisions.md
- architecture/impacted-systems.md
- governance/delivery-constitution.md
- epics/` in full.
If `- input/brs.md
- input/architecture.md
- architecture/ui-specification.md` is not empty, read those files in full as well.
If `computed_inputs` is present, read every path listed there.

**Critical reads for this action:**
- `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/epic.md` - the epic overview with scope and traceability
- `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/implementation-contract.md` - the technical contract with entities, APIs, events, rules

These files already exist (created by the previous action). Read them in full - they are your primary source for story content.

Do not start writing until all inputs are read completely.

### Step 2 - Extract scope and contract details

From `epic.md`, extract:
- features and their requirement mappings
- in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries
- dependencies and risks

From `implementation-contract.md`, extract:
- data entities, fields, and state machines
- API endpoints and schemas
- events and payload schemas
- business rules and constraints
- non-functional targets
- UI surfaces, page status, route ownership, and blocking dependencies when present
- external integrations, provider contracts, callback flows, retry/fallback rules, idempotency keys, and observability/audit obligations when present

If the implementation contract still contains unresolved blocking open design questions for required epic scope, stop and report the blocker instead of generating stories prematurely.

### Step 3 - Plan stories

Map features to stories:
- At least one story per feature (F-NNN) from the epic overview
- Split features that span multiple layers into layer-specific stories
- Add technical enablement stories for `create-new` decisions (from the contract)

During story planning, apply these decomposition rules before writing:

- **External integration rule:** if a feature or requirement depends on a named external provider or partner API, create a dedicated integration or adapter story that owns provider contract handling, timeout or retry behavior, fallback behavior, and emitted audit or observability effects
- **UI propagation rule:** if the epic contract contains `## UI Surface` entries for this feature, create dedicated frontend stories for those pages or modules; do not rely on backend or platform stories as the only implementation evidence
- **Callback and state-machine rule:** if the contract contains callback validation, asynchronous confirmation, or lifecycle state transitions, create dedicated stories for those behaviors when they would otherwise overload a general e2e story
- **Platform split rule:** when audit append, observability, metrics dashboard, notifications, or shared platform work touch different components or acceptance criteria, prefer separate stories instead of one omnibus platform story
- **Non-spike ownership rule:** if you include a spike or e2e story, plan at least one non-spike implementation story for each Must requirement it touches unless the requirement is explicitly deferred

If these rules imply more than one story for a feature, split the feature now rather than relying on coverage repair later.

### Step 4 - Create story files

For each story, create `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/stories/S-NNN.N-<slug>.md` using `.b2s/artifact-templates/lean-story.md`, where `<slug>` is a short kebab-case summary of the story title (e.g. `S-001.3-application-form-ui.md`).
Also create `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/stories/S-NNN.N-<slug>.agent.yaml` using `.b2s/artifact-templates/story-agent-contract.yaml`.

**CRITICAL - exact section structure required by the validator. Stories that deviate from this structure WILL be rejected and force a full regeneration cycle.**

Each story file MUST contain these sections in this order, using these exact heading names:

```text
# S-NNN.N - {{title}}

## Metadata
## User Story
## Business Context
## Linked Requirements
## Requirements Implemented
## Requirements Referenced
## In Scope
## Implementation Guidance
## Dependency Contracts
## UI Behaviour
## Acceptance Criteria
## Test Expectations
## Required Tests
## Out of Scope
## Dependencies
## Open Questions
```

`## UI Behaviour` is included only when Layers includes Frontend and the implementation contract contains `## UI Surface`.

### Step 5 - Self-verify before writing

Before writing any file, verify each story against this checklist:

- [ ] Metadata table has `Story Type`, `Actor`, and `Layers`
- [ ] `## User Story` contains "As a", a named actor, "so that", and is 20+ characters
- [ ] `## Business Context` has at least 2 full sentences
- [ ] `## Linked Requirements` exists as its own markdown table
- [ ] `## Requirements Implemented` is explicit
- [ ] `## Requirements Referenced` captures behavior mentioned but owned elsewhere
- [ ] `## In Scope` lists concrete behavior, not vague themes
- [ ] `## Implementation Guidance` references the implementation contract
- [ ] `## Dependency Contracts` declares consumed API, event, schema, or UI contracts when dependencies exist
- [ ] `## Acceptance Criteria` uses AC headings with `[test-type] [criticality] [automation]`
- [ ] Each AC has a `gherkin` block with `Scenario:` and at least one `Then`
- [ ] At least 3 scenarios exist, and more for integration or state-heavy stories
- [ ] `## Test Expectations` exists as a table
- [ ] `## Required Tests` exists and names concrete minimum tests
- [ ] `## Out of Scope` exists
- [ ] `## Dependencies` exists
- [ ] `## Open Questions` exists
- [ ] No placeholder text remains
- [ ] Paired `.agent.yaml` exists and includes scope, dependencies, contract details, and required tests

If you cannot produce a story at this quality level, do NOT write a skeletal stub.

### Step 6 - Verify traceability

After writing, cross-check:
- every requirement mapped to this epic is referenced by at least one story
- every Must requirement mapped to this epic is directly implemented by at least one non-spike story unless the epic context explicitly marks it deferred
- every linked requirement title matches the canonical title
- each story's business behavior matches the linked requirement meaning
- blocking open questions are present in the relevant story
- the `.agent.yaml` contract does not contradict the markdown story
- external integrations, dashboards, callbacks, fallback behavior, and platform cross-cutting concerns have explicit owning stories when those surfaces exist in the implementation contract

## Output requirements

Write story files to `epics/E-002-scoring-explainability/stories/`. If a file with the same story ID prefix already exists (e.g. `S-002.0-scoring-e2e.md`), update it in place. Otherwise create `S-NNN.N-<slug>.md`.
Same rule for agent contracts: update existing `S-NNN.N-*.agent.yaml` if present, otherwise create `S-NNN.N-<slug>.agent.yaml`.

Do NOT modify `epic.md` or `implementation-contract.md` - they already exist.

## Done criteria

- [ ] Every feature (F-NNN) has at least one story
- [ ] Every story has canonical requirement traceability
- [ ] Every story has a paired `.agent.yaml` contract
- [ ] Every story has Gherkin acceptance criteria with test type annotations
- [ ] Every story has Business Context, Implementation Guidance, and Test Expectations
- [ ] Every story distinguishes implemented vs referenced requirements
- [ ] Open questions are propagated to the right stories
- [ ] Stories collectively cover all requirements for the epic
- [ ] If solution decisions exist, every `create-new` decision has a corresponding story
- [ ] External integrations and UI surfaces from impacted systems / solution decisions are not hidden inside generic e2e stories
- [ ] Must requirements are not implemented only by spike / POC / exploration stories unless explicitly deferred
- [ ] If solution decisions or repo context exist, each story has `## Technical Scope`
- [ ] No placeholder text remains

## Stop conditions

- If `epic.md` does not exist for the current epic, stop and report the blocker
- If `implementation-contract.md` does not exist for the current epic, stop and report the blocker

## Notes for the staged engine

- Do not mention event completion, result files, or dispatcher status
- This prompt writes stories for one epic per invocation when per-item mode is active
- Validation and state updates are handled by the `.b2s` engine
